what: CG Oncology is developing cretostimogene, a virus-based treatment delivered into the bladder for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer in patients whose disease no longer responds to standard treatment.
customers: Urologists treating bladder cancer, once and if the treatment is approved.
moat: Late-stage clinical data in a bladder cancer population with few options, where the current standard is a decades-old vaccine in chronic short supply.
risks: A $238M net loss on $6M of revenue: there is no product yet
The entire value rests on one trial programme and one regulatory decision
If the treatment is not approved, very little of the current valuation is supported
opportunities: $742M of cash against $7M of debt, which funds the programme through approval
Analysts see about 34% upside, with 13 covering the stock
The standard treatment has been in shortage for years, which leaves an unusually open market
watch: The regulatory filing and approval decision for cretostimogene.
